title: Christa Ingabire
text:
I am a data scientist and data engineer currently pursuing a Master’s in Data Science at the University of British Columbia. My path into data science began through computer science. I studied computer science and business analytics at Saint Mary’s University of Minnesota before beginning my career in the Twin Cities.
At Logisolve, a technology consulting company, I worked across software development and data-related problems, including SQL reporting systems, transactional data flows, and backend integrations.
I later returned to Kigali and joined the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB) as a data engineer. There, I worked with administrative data supporting large social protection programs, including health insurance and long-term savings systems.

title: Christa Ingabire
text:
Why data science
My experience at RSSB in Kigali changed how I thought about data. Building a reliable pipeline can tell us what happened. A dashboard can reveal where something changed. But many important questions require something more: Why did it change? Which intervention caused it? Would the same intervention work for another population?
Those questions pushed my interests beyond data infrastructure toward statistics, causal reasoning, and machine learning.
I am now developing those foundations through graduate study at UBC while continuing to explore data engineering, applied statistics, machine learning, and the design of trustworthy data systems.

Outside of data science
When I am not at my desk, I am reading, writing, or always trying new cafés and restaurants wherever I am. I love connecting with people, so do not hesitate to reach out.

title: Home
text:
Hi, I’m Christa Ingabire. I’m am currently pursuing a Master’s in Data Science at the University of British Columbia. Before starting graduate school, I worked as a data engineer at the Rwanda Social Security Board, in Kigali, Rwanda, where I built and maintained data pipelines supporting national social protection programs. Previously, I worked in software and data consulting in Minneapolis, Minnesota, U.S.A.
My interests sit at the intersection of data engineering, statistical learning, machine learning, and applied data science, particularly when the underlying data represents people, institutions, or public systems.
